newsitem.title: CANADA: Five die in Quebec Solar Temple cult suicide pact.
newsitem.headline: Five die in Quebec Solar Temple cult suicide pact.

text.p: Five members of a notorious doomsday cult died in a blazing house in an apparent ritual suicide pact, but spared three teenage children, Quebec police said on Sunday.

Police found the charred bodies of three women and two men on Saturday night inside a house owned by a member of the Solar Temple, an international sect which believes death by ritualized suicide leads to rebirth in a place called "Sirius."
Police identified the dead as two French women, two Swiss men and a Canadian woman and said they included the house owner, his wife and her mother.
The married couple's three teenagers, who were apparently drugged, emerged dazed and shivering from a shed near the burning house in a rural village 37 miles (60 km) southwest of Quebec City.
In 1994 and 1995, 69 Solar Temple cult members died in suspicious circumstances in grisly fires in Switzerland and Quebec.
At a news conference on Sunday, police said preliminary evidence suggested the victims died in a suicide pact.

Lt. Alain Quirion said investigators found two or three propane tanks grouped together in the house with two small electric hot plates and two containers of fire accelerant that may have been gasoline.

Police also found letters or documents in the shed that indicated the dead were prepared for some sort of "departure." The documents appeared to point to a suicide pact involving the five victims, Quirion said.
"It is a tacit pact. Even if we don't have the word suicide anywhere, effectively that seems to be the case," Quirion said.
Police said the cult was known to place great importance on astronomical events, including the spring equinox, which occurred on Friday, but the documents did not specify a date.
Quebec coroner Yvon Naud said the vitims included the owner of the house, Didier Queze, a 39-year-old Swiss national who had been living in the area for three years.
Queze and his French wife, Chantale Goupillot, 39, were found on a bed on the second floor of the house, along with Swiss Bruno Klauss, 49, and Pauline Rioux, 54, a Canadian from Quebec.
The body of Goupillot's 63-year-old French mother, Suzanne Druau, was found on a sofa on the ground floor with a plastic bag covering her head, police said.
Naud said none of the victims had bullet wounds or showed signs of extreme trauma.
Quirion said the four bodies found in the bed appeared to be arranged in a specific way, each lying perpendicular to the other with their feet touching.
"Is it in the form of a cross? Does it have a significance? Maybe. That is what we will determine today or this week," Quirion said.
He said the children, a girl aged 14 and two boys, 13 and 16, were Queze's. "The children appeared intoxicated by medication or other drugs," Quirion said.

The children were taken to a local clinic for observation and were being counselled by social workers. Police said they would be interviewing them to determine whether they had been inside the house or the shed when the fire began.
Saint Casimir Mayor Louise Douville told Reuters Queze lived in the house with his wife and three children and ran a bakery in a nearby village.
"I knew he was a member of the Solar Temple, but most people around here did not know that," Douville said.
"They were good citizens, good taxpayers and we never had any trouble with them," she said.

Police said they were contacting other known Solar Temple members in Quebec in connection with the fire. They believe about 40 Solar Temple members live in Canada's French-speaking province of 7.3 million people.

In 1994, police found the burned bodies of 48 Solar Temple members in a farmhouse and three chalets in Switzerland. At the same time in Quebec, five bodies, including that of an infant, were found in a chalet in Morin Heights, a picturesque village in the Laurentians ski resort area north of Montreal.
In December 1995, 16 other Solar Temple members were found dead in a burned house outside Grenoble, in the French Alps. Two French police officers were among the 16 dead.
